about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Lemon Ricotta Cake
recipes.summary: A soft, moist cake that gets its tenderness from ricotta and its zing from lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a 20cm round tin with baking paper.
Whisk the ricotta, eggs, caster sugar, lemon zest and juice and melted butter together in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined, then scrape into the tin.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin, then dust with icing sugar.
notes: Keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Almond Amaretti Biscuits
recipes.summary: Chewy, crackled almond biscuits with no flour at all.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper.
Whisk the egg whites in a bowl until they hold soft peaks, then fold in the almond meal, caster sugar and vanilla until a sticky dough forms.
Roll tablespoons of the dough into balls, toss in the icing sugar and set them 3cm apart on the trays.
Bake for 18 minutes, until pale golden and cracked on top. Cool on the tray, where they firm up.
notes: Gluten-free: check your icing sugar label for added starch.

recipes.title: Pears Poached in Marsala
recipes.summary: Tender pears simmered in sweet Marsala and cinnamon until glossy.
steps: Put the marsala, water, sugar, cinnamon stick and orange peel in a saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a circle of baking paper and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Lift out the pears, then boil the syrup for 5 minutes, until reduced by half. Spoon over the pears and serve warm or cold.

recipes.title: French Apple Tarte Fine
recipes.summary: Paper-thin apple slices fanned over crisp puff pastry and glazed with apricot jam.

items: 4 apple, cored and very thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the pastry in half, lay on two lined trays and prick the centres with a fork, leaving a 2cm border.
Fan the apple slices over the pastry, overlapping them. Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and the apple edges are golden.
Warm the jam with the water until runny, then brush over the hot tarts.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Pots
recipes.summary: Silky, rich chocolate custards set in little cups.
steps: Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until just steaming, then pour over the chocolate in a bowl and stir until smooth.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and salt together, then slowly whisk in the warm chocolate mixture.
Return to the pan and stir over low heat for 5 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon and reaches 75°C. Do not let it boil.
Pour into six small cups and chill until set.
notes: Food safety: the egg yolks are cooked to 75°C, so the pots are safe to serve, but keep them chilled and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Honey Lemon Madeleines
recipes.summary: Buttery little shell cakes with a honey and lemon scent, best eaten warm.
steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar, honey and lemon zest in a bowl for 3 minutes, until pale and thick.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, then the melted butter. Cover and rest the batter in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and grease a madeleine tray.
Spoon the batter into the moulds and bake for 10 minutes, until puffed and golden at the edges. Dust with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Whole Orange and Almond Cake
recipes.summary: A dense, fragrant, naturally gluten-free cake made with boiled whole oranges.
steps: Cover the whole oranges with water in a saucepan and simmer for 1 hour, until very soft. Drain, cool, halve and discard any pips, then blitz the oranges, skin and all, to a purée.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 22cm tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then stir in the orange purée, almond meal and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool and dust with icing sugar.
notes: Gluten-free. Plus 1 hour simmering the oranges, which can be done a day ahead.

recipes.title: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
recipes.summary: Crisp ridged fried dough rolled in cinnamon sugar and dunked in warm chocolate.
steps: Bring the water and butter to the boil in a saucepan, tip in the flour and beat with a wooden spoon until it forms a smooth ball.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until glossy. Spoon into a piping bag with a star nozzle.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C. Pipe 10cm lengths into the oil, snip with scissors and fry for 3 minutes, until deep golden. Drain on paper towel.
Toss the churros in the sugar and cinnamon. Warm the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth, then serve for dipping.
notes: Keep the oil at 180°C and never leave hot oil unattended.

recipes.title: Smoked Paprika Crispy Chickpeas
recipes.summary: A crunchy, salty, smoky bar snack made in a tray.

items: 800g tinned chickpeas, drained and patted dry

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt on a lined tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and deep golden. Squeeze over the lemon juice and eat the same day.

recipes.title: Thick Yoghurt Parfait with Walnut Crumb
recipes.summary: Thick yoghurt, toasted walnuts, orange segments and a thread of honey.

items: 1 orange, peeled and cut into segments

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until fragrant, then crush roughly.
Cut the orange into segments, catching any juice.
Layer the yoghurt, orange and walnuts in two glasses, then drizzle with the honey and dust with cinnamon.

recipes.title: Orange Semolina Syrup Cake
recipes.summary: A tender semolina cake soaked in an orange and cinnamon syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 20cm square tin.
Mix the semolina, flour and baking powder in a bowl. Whisk the yoghurt, caster sugar, oil, eggs and orange zest in another bowl, then combine the two.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile simmer the white sugar, water, cinnamon stick and orange juice for 8 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake.

recipes.title: Rosewater Pistachio Shortbread
recipes.summary: Crumbly buttery shortbread scented with rose and topped with green pistachios.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and icing sugar for 3 minutes, until pale. Stir in the flour, cornflour and rose water to form a soft dough.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, flatten gently and press a few pistachios into each.
Bake for 18 minutes, until just pale gold at the edges. Cool on the trays.

recipes.title: Za'atar Labneh Dip with Flatbread Crisps
recipes.summary: Thick labneh swirled with za'atar and olive oil, scooped up with crisp flatbread.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the flatbread with 1 tbsp of the olive oil and the salt, spread on a tray and bake for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Spread the labneh in a shallow bowl, swirl in the lemon juice, then top with the remaining oil and the za'atar.
Serve with the warm crisps.

recipes.title: Honey Almond Crescents
recipes.summary: Gluten-free Moroccan-style almond moons, soft and fragrant with a honey glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a tray.
Mix the almond meal, icing sugar, cinnamon, egg white and orange juice into a firm paste.
Shape tablespoons of the paste into small crescents and set them on the tray. Brush with honey and scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool on the tray.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Scones with Jam and Cream
recipes.summary: Tall, light scones for a proper afternoon tea.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and flour a tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and sugar with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the buttermilk with a knife to a soft dough.
Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Bake for 15 minutes, until risen and golden. Serve warm with the whipped cream and jam.
notes: Do not twist the cutter, so the scones rise straight.

recipes.title: Sticky Ginger Cake
recipes.summary: A dark, treacly, spicy loaf that gets stickier on day two.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a 20cm tin.
Warm the butter, golden syrup, molasses and brown sugar in a saucepan over low heat until melted, then stir in the milk.
Whisk the flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl, pour in the warm syrup mixture and beat in the egg until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Better after a day in an airtight tin.

recipes.title: Oat Soda Bread
recipes.summary: A no-yeast Irish loaf you can have on the table within the hour.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and flour a tray.
Mix the flour, oats, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl, make a well and pour in the buttermilk. Stir with a wooden spoon to a shaggy dough.
Shape into a round on the tray, cut a deep cross in the top and bake for 40 minutes, until the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack for 20 minutes before slicing.
notes: Best eaten the day it's made.

recipes.title: Apple Strudel Rolls
recipes.summary: Crisp filo rolls packed with cinnamon apples and sultanas.
steps: Cook the apple, sultanas, brown sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until the apple is just tender. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer two filo sheets, brushing each with butter, and scatter with a tablespoon of breadcrumbs.
Spoon a quarter of the filling along one long edge, roll up and place seam-side down on a lined tray. Repeat for four rolls and cut each in half.
Brush with the remaining butter and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden. Dust with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Palatschinken with Apricot Jam
recipes.summary: Thin Austrian pancakes rolled around tangy apricot jam.
steps: Whisk the flour, milk, water, eggs and salt until smooth and let the batter stand while the pan heats.
Melt a little butter in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat.
Cook for 1 minute each side, until golden and set, and stack the pancakes on a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Spread each pancake with jam, roll up and dust with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Lamington Squares
recipes.summary: Butter cake squares dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and milk.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely, then cut into 16 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl and stir in the boiling water until smooth. Dip each square in the icing, then roll in the coconut and set on a rack.
notes: Day-old cake cuts cleanest, so bake it the day before.

recipes.title: Chewy Coconut Anzac Cookies
recipes.summary: Chewy oat and coconut biscuits with a golden syrup caramel edge.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter, golden syrup and water in a small saucepan, stir in the bicarbonate of soda and pour into the dry mix.
Roll tablespoons into balls, flatten on the trays and bake for 15 minutes, until golden. They firm up as they cool.

recipes.title: Chocolate Zucchini Loaf
recipes.summary: A moist chocolate loaf with grated zucchini that keeps it tender.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil in a bowl, then stir in the zucchini.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and milk until just combined, then the chopped chocolate.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin.

recipes.title: Flourless Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.summary: Three-ingredient cookies, crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) and line a tray.
Stir the peanut butter, sugar, egg and bicarbonate of soda together until a thick dough forms.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, press with a fork and bake for 12 minutes, until set at the edges. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before moving.

recipes.title: Fudgy Walnut Brownies
recipes.summary: Dense chocolate brownies with a shiny crust and crunchy walnuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over a pan of simmering water, stirring until smooth, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the sugar and eggs, then fold in the flour, cocoa, salt and walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until the top is set but the centre still has a slight wobble. Cool before cutting.

recipes.title: Maple Roasted Pecans
recipes.summary: Crunchy pecans glazed with maple, salt and a little cayenne.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a tray.
Toss the pecans with the maple syrup, salt, cayenne and cinnamon until well coated.
Spread on the tray and roast for 15 minutes, stirring once, until glossy and fragrant. Cool completely so they crisp.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Tortilla Crisps with Chocolate Dip
recipes.summary: Crunchy cinnamon sugar tortilla triangles with a warm chocolate sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the tortilla wedges with butter, toss in the sugar and cinnamon and spread on two trays.
Bake for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Warm the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth. Serve with the crisps.

recipes.title: Arroz con Leche
recipes.summary: Creamy cinnamon rice pudding, served warm or chilled.
steps: Simmer the rice with the water and cinnamon stick in a saucepan for 10 minutes, until the water is mostly absorbed.
Add the milk, sugar and raisins and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick, stir in the vanilla and dust with ground cinnamon.
notes: Food safety: cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Coconut Rum Raisin Rice Pudding
recipes.summary: Rice simmered in coconut milk with warm spices and rum-soaked raisins.
steps: Warm the raisins and rum in a small pan for 2 minutes, then set aside to soak.
Simmer the rice, coconut milk, water, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a saucepan over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Stir through the raisins and rum and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Cornflour Sandwich Biscuits
recipes.summary: Melt-in-the-mouth shortbread sandwiched with jam, inspired by South American alfajores.
steps: Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then beat in the yolks.
Stir in the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder to a soft dough. Wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Roll the dough 5mm thick, cut 5cm rounds and bake on lined trays for 12 minutes, until pale. Cool.
Sandwich pairs with jam and roll the edges in the coconut.

recipes.title: Crisp Plantain Tostones
recipes.summary: Twice-fried green plantain discs with lime salt, great with any dip.

items: 3 plantain, peeled and cut into thick rounds

steps: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 160°C and fry the plantain rounds for 3 minutes each side, until pale gold. Drain.
Press each round flat with the bottom of a glass.
Raise the oil to 180°C and fry again for 2 minutes each side, until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Toss with the salt, lime juice and garlic and serve hot.

recipes.title: Coconut Bake
recipes.summary: A soft, slightly sweet Caribbean bread made with coconut milk.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl, then stir in the warm coconut milk and butter to form a dough.
Knead on a floured bench for 8 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Cover and prove in a warm spot.
Divide into 8, flatten into rounds and set on a lined tray. Rest for 15 minutes.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
notes: Plus 1 hour proving and 15 minutes resting.

recipes.title: White Bean Panzanella
recipes.summary: Crusty bread, ripe tomatoes and creamy beans soaked in a sharp red wine dressing.
steps: Toss the bread with 1 tbsp of the oil and toast in a hot frying pan for 5 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Combine the tomatoes, beans, cucumber and onion in a large bowl.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar and salt, pour over the salad, add the bread and basil, and toss. Rest for 10 minutes so the bread soaks up the juices.

recipes.title: Pesto Mozzarella Pressed Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Crisp, golden panini filled with melting mozzarella, pesto and tomato.
steps: Spread the pesto on two slices of bread and top with mozzarella and tomato, then the other slices.
Brush the outsides with olive oil.
Cook in a hot frying pan, pressing down with a plate, for 4 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
notes: Vegetarian: check the pesto label for a vegetarian hard cheese.

recipes.title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
recipes.summary: A pantry salad of tuna, creamy beans, red onion and parsley.
steps: Rinse the beans and drain well.
Combine the beans with the tuna, onion, parsley and capers in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt and toss through gently until just coated. Serve at room temperature.
notes: Food safety: tinned tuna should be used by 2 days after opening and kept chilled; cooked fish is safe at 63°C.

recipes.title: Tuna Niçoise Platter
recipes.summary: Classic French salad of tuna, soft-boiled eggs, beans, potatoes and olives.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes. Drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are just firm, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, mustard and vinegar. Arrange the potatoes, beans, tuna, olives, tomatoes and eggs on a platter and drizzle with the dressing.
notes: Food safety: boiled eggs should have fully set whites and yolks; tuna from a tin is cooked and flakes easily.

recipes.title: Leek and Goat Cheese Tart
recipes.summary: Sweet slow-cooked leeks and tangy goat cheese in a crisp pastry case.
steps: Cook the leeks in the butter in a frying pan over low heat for 12 minutes, until soft and sweet.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line a 24cm tart tin with the pastry and prick the base.
Whisk the eggs and cream. Spread the leeks over the pastry, scatter with the goat cheese and thyme and pour over the egg mixture.
Bake for 35 minutes, until puffed and golden with a firm centre.
notes: Food safety: the egg filling is cooked through when the centre is firm, not wobbly.

recipes.title: Croque Monsieur
recipes.summary: Grilled ham and gruyère sandwich under a bubbling cheesy béchamel.
steps: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until the sauce thickens. Season with nutmeg and a third of the gruyère.
Spread two slices of bread with mustard, top with the ham, half the remaining gruyère and the other slices.
Place on a tray, spoon over the sauce and scatter with the rest of the gruyère.
Grill at 220°C for 10 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
notes: Food safety: ham is cooked and ready to eat; heat the sandwich until it is steaming hot in the middle.

recipes.title: Tortilla Española Wedges
recipes.summary: A thick Spanish potato and onion omelette, cooked until just set.
steps: Cook the potato and onion in the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, turning, until very tender but not browned. Drain, saving 1 tbsp of the oil.
Beat the eggs and salt in a large bowl, stir in the potato mixture and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the saved oil in the pan, add the mixture and cook over low heat for 8 minutes, until the base is golden and most of the egg is set.
Flip with a plate and cook for 4 minutes more, until the centre is cooked through. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Food safety: egg must be fully cooked through, with no runny centre.

recipes.title: Chilled Gazpacho
recipes.summary: A cold Andalusian tomato and capsicum soup that needs no cooking.
steps: Blend the tomato, cucumber, capsicum, garlic, bread, vinegar and salt in batches until very smooth.
With the blender running, stream in the oil until emulsified.
Strain if you like, then chill until very cold. Taste and add more salt or vinegar.

recipes.title: Horiatiki Salad with Grilled Halloumi
recipes.summary: Chunky tomato and cucumber salad topped with golden halloumi.
steps: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and oregano, pour over and toss.
Fry the halloumi in a dry non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden. Serve on top.

recipes.title: Avgolemono Orzo Soup
recipes.summary: A bright, silky lemon soup with shredded chicken and orzo.
steps: Simmer the chicken, stock, carrot and onion in a large pot for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre. Lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the orzo to the stock and cook for 8 minutes, until tender.

Whisk the eggs and lemon juice, then slowly ladle in a cup of hot stock, whisking. Stir back into the pot off the heat with the chicken and dill, and warm gently until the soup thickens slightly, without boiling.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre and have no pink meat. Eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Fattoush with Sumac Chickpeas
recipes.summary: Crisp pita and garden vegetables with a lemony sumac dressing and spiced chickpeas.
steps: Toss the pita with 1 tbsp oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 10 minutes, until crisp.
Fry the chickpeas in 1 tbsp oil with 1 tsp sumac for 5 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, lettuce and mint with the lemon juice, remaining oil and remaining sumac. Top with the pita and chickpeas just before serving.

recipes.title: Cumin Carrot Salad with Parsley
recipes.summary: Tender carrots in a garlicky cumin and lemon dressing, served cold.
steps: Boil the carrots in salted water for 10 minutes, until just tender. Drain.
Toss with the garlic, cumin, paprika, oil, lemon juice and salt while still warm.
Chill, then stir through the parsley before serving.

recipes.title: Ploughman's Toastie
recipes.summary: Sharp cheddar, pickle and apple in a crisp toastie.
steps: Butter the bread on the outside.
Spread pickle inside two slices and top with cheddar and apple, then the other slices.
Cook in a frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.

recipes.title: Coronation Chicken Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Cold poached chicken in a mild curry mayo with sultanas and almonds.
steps: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 15 minutes, until it reaches 75°C in the centre and the juices run clear. Cool completely, then shred.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, curry powder and chutney, then fold in the chicken, sultanas and almonds.
Fill the bread with salad leaves and the chicken mixture.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until 75°C inside, cool quickly and keep refrigerated; eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Buttery Leek Soup with Chives
recipes.summary: A velvety Irish-style soup with sweet leeks and buttery potato.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the leeks for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potato falls apart.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk and pepper and heat until steaming. Top with chives.

recipes.title: Kartoffelpuffer with Apple Sauce
recipes.summary: Crisp, lacy potato pancakes with warm apple sauce on the side.
steps: Squeeze as much liquid as you can out of the grated potato in a clean tea towel, then mix with the onion, eggs, flour and salt.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Drop in heaped tablespoons and flatten.
Fry for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp, and drain on paper towel. Serve with the apple sauce and sour cream.

recipes.title: Bratwurst and Sauerkraut Rolls
recipes.summary: Browned bratwurst in a soft roll with sauerkraut and sweet mustard.
steps: Fry the bratwurst in a pan with a little oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and the centre reaches 75°C.
Add the onion for the last 8 minutes and cook until soft and golden.
Warm the sauerkraut in the pan for 2 minutes, until steaming. Fill the rolls with a sausage, onions, sauerkraut and mustard.
notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside.

recipes.title: Corn and Zucchini Fritters with Feta
recipes.summary: Golden fritters packed with sweet corn, zucchini and salty feta.
steps: Mix the zucchini, corn, flour, eggs, milk, feta and spring onion in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry heaped spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with the yoghurt.

recipes.title: Lemon Pepper Chicken Burgers
recipes.summary: Crispy-coated chicken on a toasted bun with lettuce and tangy mayo.

items: 500g chicken breast, sliced into 4 thin steaks

steps: Mix the panko, pepper and lemon zest on a plate and beat the egg in a shallow bowl. Dip each chicken piece in egg, then crumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the chicken for 6 minutes each side, until golden and the centre reaches 75°C.
Toast the buns until golden, spread with mayonnaise and fill with lettuce, tomato and chicken.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part and have no pink meat.
